import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from scipy.optimize import curve_fit
from scipy.signal import savgol_filter
def load(f):
    d=pd.read_csv(f); return d.shift_cm1.values.astype(float), d.intensity.values.astype(float)
def lor(x,A,x0,w): return A*(w/2)**2/((x-x0)**2+(w/2)**2)
def mk(n):
    def m(x,c0,c1,*p):
        y=c0+c1*(x-400)
        for i in range(n):
            A,x0,w=p[3*i:3*i+3]; y=y+lor(x,A,x0,w)
        return y
    return m
def fit(x,y,p0,n,lo,hi):
    s=(x>=lo)&(x<=hi); xs,ys=x[s],y[s]
    m=mk(n)
    p0=[np.percentile(ys,5),0]+p0
    lb=[-np.inf,-np.inf]+[0,lo,0.5]*n; ub=[np.inf,np.inf]+[np.inf,hi,60]*n
    popt,pcov=curve_fit(m,xs,ys,p0=p0,bounds=(lb,ub),maxfev=20000)
    res=ys-m(xs,*popt); dof=len(xs)-len(popt)
    perr=np.sqrt(np.diag(pcov))
    return popt,perr,res,xs
for f in ["spectrum_day1.csv","spectrum_day2.csv"]:
    x,y=load(f)
    print("\n==",f)
    # E2g + A1g window 365-425

caveats: The Si line should read 520.7 cm-1 (the standard room-temperature value, not checked against a source here). If so, day 1 is offset by about -0.7 cm-1 and day 2 by about +1.8 cm-1. A 2.5 cm-1 change in calibration is much larger than typical calibration scatter (a few tenths of a cm-1), so the spectrometer was likely re-zeroed or drifted between sessions.
Laser heating red-shifts Raman lines, so it cannot explain the common shift, which goes up. The Si line moving up too rules out a local temperature change of the flake.

Adsorbate doping and strain in MoS2 are expected to produce shifts of the order of 1 cm-1 or less (Chakraborty et al. 2012; Conley et al. 2013, Nano Lett. 13, 3626, both recalled from memory). A relative shift below about 0.1 cm-1 therefore argues against a meaningful change, but that depends on the literature values being right.
Day 2 was sampled at 0.66 cm-1 per point against 0.53 cm-1 on day 1. Fitted widths and positions on day 2 are less well resolved, so their errors are probably understated.
Absolute intensities are not comparable between sessions (background changed by about 38%; laser power and collection were not reported). Intensity ratios are only a weak check here.

The fitting was done inline with Lorentzians and a linear baseline, not with the skill's validated scripts (the scripts and reference notes are outside this working folder, which the operator told me not to read). Errors are fit-covariance only, with no systematic term added.

The matching of the positions to 2H-MoS2 uses literature values recalled from memory (Lee et al. 2010; Chakraborty et al. 2012; Conley et al. 2013), not checked against the papers in this environment.

Why do the two files have different point spacing (0.53 vs 0.66 cm-1)? Did the grating, spectral range, or resolution setting change?
Were laser power, objective, integration time, and acquisition settings the same on both days? The background is about 38% higher on day 2.
Was the same spot relocated from an optical image or from stage coordinates? A small spatial offset can change the local layer number or strain, though the observables here show no such change.
